name: Lagos Lagoon & Barrier Coast
summary: Shallow lagoon behind Lagos barrier islands; Atlantic access via Lekki and Lagos harbour creeks.
description: The lagoon stretches from Badagry through metropolitan Lagos to the Lekki peninsula. It receives urban drainage from Lagos and Ogun, supports sand mining and fishing, and connects to the Atlantic through dredged channels. Victoria Island and Lekki sit on former barrier islands and reclaimed land.
economy: Port access, sand mining, urban drainage, ferry transport, fisheries.
ecology: Brackish water, degraded mangroves, urban pollution, siltation.
environment: Coastal erosion on Victoria Island and Elegushi; wastewater and dredging pressure.
significance: Historic harbour of Eko; Lekki Deep Sea Port gateway.

name: Niger Delta Estuary
summary: Africa's largest delta empties through Forcados, Escravos, Bonny, and other distributaries into the Gulf of Guinea.
description: The Niger River splits into a maze of creeks, mangrove channels, and sandbars across Delta, Bayelsa, and Rivers states. Oil terminals, artisanal fisheries, and riverine communities depend on these channels. Pollution and gas flaring have degraded parts of the delta wetlands.
economy: Offshore oil, artisanal fishing, palm produce, river transport.
ecology: Mangrove forest, turtles, seasonal floodplains, high biodiversity.
environment: Oil spills, gas flaring, mangrove loss, subsidence in some areas.
significance: National oil wealth centre; UNESCO Ramsar interest in parts of the delta.

name: Cross River Estuary
summary: Tidal estuary at Calabar where the Cross River meets the Atlantic; eastern trade gateway.
description: The Cross River estuary has served Efik and European trade since the 15th century. Calabar port sits on the estuary; silting and channel maintenance affect draft. The estuary links to Cameroon via historical trade routes and the Bakassi peninsula context.
economy: General cargo, regional export, fishing, limited tourism.
ecology: Mangrove fringe, estuarine fisheries, turtle nesting in nearby beaches.
environment: Channel siltation; erosion on some eastern beaches.
significance: Eastern seaport; historic Efik harbour; Cameroon border trade.

name: Forcados Oil Terminal
summary: Major Niger Delta crude loading terminal on the Forcados River mouth.
description: Forcados terminal handles export crude from western delta fields via the Forcados pipeline system. Attacks and sabotage have periodically shut the terminal; dredged channels link to open sea tanker anchorage.
economy: Crude oil export, tanker loading, oil-field logistics.
environment: Oil spill risk; pipeline vandalism history.

name: Bonny Oil Terminal
summary: Bonny Island hosts Nigeria LNG and associated oil export infrastructure.
description: Bonny Island in Rivers State is a major energy export node: NLNG trains, crude loading, and oil-service traffic. The Bonny River channel connects Port Harcourt and Onne to the Atlantic.
economy: LNG export, crude oil, oil services, shipping.
ecology: Island and mangrove interface; industrial footprint.
significance: Nigeria LNG headquarters; eastern delta energy hub.

name: Escravos Oil Terminal
summary: Chevron-operated Escravos terminal exports crude and supports gas projects in the western delta.
description: Escravos terminal on the Escravos River serves western delta oil and gas fields. Warri port and the Escravos–Warri road corridor link the terminal to the delta industrial belt.
economy: Crude export, gas processing, delta logistics.
ecology: Mangrove creeks; gas flare legacy in region.
environment: Pollution pressure in western delta wetlands.
significance: Major western delta export point; Warri industrial link.

name: Lagos Coastal Erosion Belt
summary: Victoria Island, Lekki, and Alpha Beach areas face chronic Atlantic erosion and storm surge.
description: Sand mining, groynes, and sea-level rise interact along the Lagos open coast. Erosion threatens roads, estates, and beaches; Lagos State runs periodic beach nourishment and protection works.
economy: Tourism, real estate, coastal engineering contracts.
ecology: Intertidal zone loss; turtle nesting pressure on remaining beaches.
environment: Sea-level rise, storm surge, sand mining, coastal squeeze.
significance: Most urbanised erosion front in Nigeria.

name: Niger Delta Mangrove Belt
summary: West Africa's largest mangrove tract — carbon store, fisheries nursery, and pollution-sensitive wetland.
description: Rhizophora and Avicennia mangroves fringe delta creeks from Ondo through Bayelsa. Oil spills, deforestation for firewood, and land reclamation have reduced cover; restoration projects operate in parts of Rivers and Delta.
ecology: Fish nursery, carbon sequestration, migratory birds, biodiversity hotspot.
environment: Oil pollution, mangrove loss, gas flaring, climate vulnerability.
significance: National blue-carbon asset; livelihood base for riverine communities.

name: Bakassi Peninsula
summary: Marshy peninsula at the Nigeria–Cameroon border; ICJ transfer to Cameroon (2008) with residual Nigerian communities.
description: Bakassi sits on the Cross River estuary approach to the Atlantic. Fishing communities, border security, and mangrove wetlands define the area. The peninsula illustrates maritime boundary and livelihood issues on the eastern coast.
economy: Artisanal fishing, cross-border trade, security patrols.
significance: ICJ boundary case; eastern maritime frontier.

name: Badagry Heritage Coast
summary: Badagry was a major 18th–19th century slave-export port; heritage sites line the lagoon coast.
description: Badagry's wharf, museum, and Point of No Return memorial mark the transatlantic slave trade era. The town sits on the western lagoon coast near the Benin border and remains a domestic tourism destination.
ecology: Lagoon and creek fisheries; mangrove patches.
significance: UNESCO memory route interest; national heritage tourism.
